name: UAV-X: Resilient BVLOS Swarm Challenge
desc: A national engineering challenge to build autonomous UAV swarms that maintain resilient BVLOS communication while executing a disaster response mission, taking teams from simulation to a field-ready design under expert mentorship.
about: UAV-X is Grand Challenge of the PUSHPAK Grand Challenge 2026, a national innovation challenge under the PUSHPAK: National Mission on Drone Technology, funded by MeitY, Government of India, hosted by IIT Bombay, and presented by IISERB in collaboration with IISER Bhopal. Unlike a conventional hackathon or idea competition, this challenge takes promising technical concepts through evaluation, mentoring, and deployment-oriented development. Teams develop autonomous UAV swarms capable of maintaining resilient beyond visual line-of-sight (BVLOS) communication while executing a disaster response mission, surveying disaster zones, relaying data through a multi-hop aerial network, and reconfiguring on the fly as UAVs fail or lose connectivity. Selected winning teams get invited to a post-challenge Prototype Development Support Programme to bridge the gap between simulation and real-world deployment.
structure:
Eligibility: Open to UG and PG college students, PhD and postdoctoral research scholars, and startups or early-stage teams working in aerospace, robotics, computer science, electronics, or communication systems. Project staff, research staff, consultants, or interns directly engaged with the PUSHPAK Project or the organizing institutions are not eligible.

Team size: Up to 5 members per team.

Stage 1 – Preliminary Design Verification
All registered teams submit a 6-8 page technical proposal with software architecture, a working proof-of-concept simulation, source code, installation instructions, and a demo video. Up to 15 teams qualify and receive INR 1 Lakh each.

Stage 2 – Technical Challenge
Qualified teams receive advanced disaster scenarios with hidden disturbances such as UAV failures and communication outages, and submit final source code, a technical report, simulation logs, and a demo video. The top 10 teams qualify for the finale.

Stage 3 – Grand Finale
Finalist teams present their approach and execute a previously unseen disaster-response scenario before the jury at Techfest, IIT Bombay. Up to 5 winning teams are selected and considered for further funding, mentoring, and prototype support.

rules:
Teams must register on the official Techfest website and submit all entries via email; no submission portals or forms are used.
Project staff, research staff, consultants, or interns directly engaged with the PUSHPAK Project or organizing institutions are not eligible; any team found to include an ineligible participant may be disqualified at any stage.
Participants are solely responsible for the accuracy, originality, technical feasibility, safety, and performance of their submissions.
Proposed solutions must comply with all applicable laws, aviation requirements, and safety protocols in India; participants are responsible for obtaining any permissions needed for testing or demonstration.
Participants retain ownership of their intellectual property unless otherwise agreed under the Grand Challenge terms; submissions must not infringe on third-party IP.
Unless stated otherwise, all participation expenses, including development, testing, travel, and accommodation, are borne by the participating teams.
The decision of the evaluation committee is final and binding; no correspondence regarding evaluation or ranking will be entertained.
The organizers reserve the right to modify, postpone, or cancel the Grand Challenge or any stage, with changes communicated through official channels.
The process for disbursement of prize money will be communicated at a later stage; participating teams are requested to regularly check the official website and their registered email for updates.
faq:
Q: Who can participate?
A:UG and PG college students from aerospace, robotics, computer science, electronics/communication, electrical, or mechanical engineering; PhD and postdoctoral research scholars in unmanned aerial systems, swarm robotics, or wireless networking; and startups or early-stage teams building drones or autonomy stacks.

Q: What's the team size?
A:Up to 5 members per team.

Q: Is anyone excluded from participating?
A:Yes. Project staff, research staff, consultants, interns, or other personnel directly engaged with the PUSHPAK Project, Drone Centre, or the organizing/host institutions are not eligible, whether participating individually or as part of a team.

Q: What exactly are we building?
A:An autonomous UAV swarm that surveys disaster locations, maintains end-to-end communication with a Ground Control Station through a resilient multi-hop aerial network, and reconfigures dynamically as UAVs fail or lose connectivity, all in simulation.

Q: Do we need physical drones?
A:No. The challenge is simulation-first, keeping the barrier to entry low. Participants can use any open-source framework such as PX4 SITL, ArduPilot SITL, Gazebo, AirSim, Isaac Sim, or ROS/ROS 2.

Q: How many stages are there?
A:Three: Preliminary Design Verification, Technical Challenge, and the Grand Finale at Techfest, IIT Bombay.

Q: How many teams advance at each stage?
A:Roughly 15 teams qualify from Stage 1, the top 10 from Stage 2, and up to 5 winning teams are selected at the Finale.

Q: How do we submit our proposals?
A:Entirely via email to pushpak_gc2026@aero.iitb.ac.in. There are no submission links; every stage is handled through email correspondence.

Q: Is there funding at each stage?
A:Yes. Stage 1 qualifiers receive INR 1 Lakh each. Stage 2 qualifiers get domestic travel and accommodation support (as per IIT Bombay guidelines). Stage 3 winners receive prize money ranging from INR 1.5 Lakh to INR 3 Lakh.

Q: How is the final solution evaluated?
A:Across seven weighted criteria: mission completion (25%), communication resilience (25%), autonomous relay and role management (20%), fault recovery and swarm reconfiguration (15%), safety and collision avoidance (10%), and innovation and technical merit (5%).

Q: What happens after the finale?
A:Up to 5 winning teams are invited to a dedicated Prototype Development Support Programme starting December 2026, with access to further funding, technical mentoring, and IIT Bombay resources for building and testing.
